newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia builders want bond support retained.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia builders want bond support retained.

text.p: A leading Australian industry group on Thursday said that a government decision to axe infrastructure bonds could jeopardise the fate of vital and lucrative development projects.
The Australian Constructors Association urged a replacement scheme soon to foster future infrastructure development, worth billions of dollars a year.

"Unquestionably, there's a lot of infrastructure projects that are being considered in Australia, worth billions and billions of dollars, and it's (ending the bonds scheme) obviously got to have an influence," association president and
Leighton Holdings Ltd chief Wal King told reporters.
"It is irrefutable that when infrastructure is done then development follows."
The government said in February it would abolish the infrastructure bonds scheme after a study found the programme was being exploited for tax minimisation.
Under the scheme, a project developer could issue, with government approval, bonds whose interest attracted no tax.
Lenders therefore were able to offer a lower interest rate and although the developer could not claim the interest expense against income, the bottom line was a tax-break for the approved project.
Treasurer Peter Costello has said the government would consider alternative schemes, but has given no further details.
